content.title: About
content.content: Meat loaf is a baked dish made from ground meat, usually beef or a beef‑pork blend, mixed with eggs, breadcrumbs, onion and spices. It is shaped like a loaf, has a dense texture and a savory aroma, and is served in slices either hot or cold.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the 19th century as a way to use leftover meat.
The classic recipe used only beef and beef broth, but today versions with turkey, chicken or even vegetarian substitutes are common.
Meat loaf is often paired with tomato sauce, mustard or sweet barbecue glaze.
In some regions it is called "meat cake" because of its loaf‑like shape.
There is a "meat loaf in batter" variant where the meat mixture is coated in a light batter and baked to a golden crust.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The ground meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune response and wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of fats and carbohydrates makes meat loaf a good source of sustained energy for active individuals.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large amounts of fatty meat can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Salt and preservatives
items.content: Commercial meat loaves often contain added salt and nitrites, which should be limited.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some people may have an allergy or intolerance to specific types of meat.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked ground meat may harbor pathogenic bacteria, so proper cooking temperature is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the meat loaf thinly and serve hot with a sauce, in sandwiches, atop salads, or as a side to soups. It can also be chilled, cubed, and used for appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked meat loaf in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized pieces – up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
